UI-08 (keyboard shortcuts and accessible UI): extended viewer.ts's keyHandler with Home/End (first/last page), bare +/- (zoom -- deliberately not Ctrl+, which is the browser's own page-zoom shortcut), Ctrl/Cmd+Z and +Shift+Z (undo/redo via two new HistoryHandle methods, triggerUndo/triggerRedo, that are exactly button.click() so a shortcut can never act past what the button's own disabled state already allows), and 'c' (toggle UI-05's Compare view). Added title/aria-label to toolbar buttons naming their shortcuts. Found and fixed a real, pre-existing app bug while scoping this: isTypingTarget only checked INPUT/TEXTAREA tag names, not contentEditable, so pressing arrow keys while editing a span's text (a contenteditable div, not an INPUT) ALSO navigated pages and silently broke caret movement via the handler's own preventDefault -- fixed by also checking target.isContentEditable. Found and fixed a second bug, this time in the test suite: _commit_edit only waited for editing to visibly end (synchronous, before the network request or reloadDocument() finish), which raced a UI-05 test (check/uncheck the diff toggle) on Windows CI specifically -- a delayed second compare.show() call from the edit's own late-finishing reload reset the checkbox mid-test. Fixed once at the source (_commit_edit now waits for a .pw-history-entry to appear, the real last effect of reloadDocument() completing) rather than patched per call site. Also caught, this session: ruff format --check hadn't actually been run locally since the UI-04 session (only ruff check had) -- two UI-05 files were unformatted, which is exactly what made CI run #28 fail on the lint job; reformatted and confirmed clean, and ruff format --check is now a permanent part of the local gate routine. 5 new Playwright tests. openQuestions: ALWAYS run `python3 -m ruff format --check engine cli tools tests server` as part of the local gate, not just `python3 -m ruff check .` -- these are two separate CI jobs' worth of checks (lint job runs both `ruff check .` AND `ruff format --check ...` as separate steps) and only running the first one left a real formatting violation undetected for a full push-and-fail cycle (UI-05's commit 62f4a8c). Add this reminder to whatever session-start checklist exists next time one is written.

Any Playwright test that acts on the UI immediately after `_commit_edit` (or any helper whose done-ness is inferred from an *intermediate* synchronous DOM change rather than the actual async chain's final effect) needs to either wait for that chain's real last effect, or rely on an action (like `page.click()`) whose own actionability wait happens to absorb the race. `_commit_edit` itself now waits for `.pw-history-entry` to appear as its last step specifically so every current and future caller gets this for free -- don't reintroduce a bare `_NOT_EDITING`-only wait in a new helper without the same consideration.

isTypingTarget (viewer.ts) checks `target.isContentEditable`, not just INPUT/TEXTAREA tag names -- this is the correct general check for 'is the user typing somewhere', since isContentEditable is true for a contenteditable element AND its descendants (unlike a tag-name check, which only matches the exact element). Any FUTURE editable UI surface in this app (not just overlay.ts's span boxes) gets this guard for free as long as it's built on contenteditable or a real INPUT/TEXTAREA -- don't add a new bespoke text-entry mechanism without checking it's covered.

UI-08's keyboard shortcuts are deliberately NOT documented anywhere in the UI itself (no shortcuts-help modal/panel) -- only via each button's `title` attribute (hover tooltip) and aria-label. This matches the feature's S-sizing in tracker/features.json; a discoverable shortcuts reference (e.g. a '?' key opening a cheat-sheet overlay) was considered and deliberately not built, since it would have pushed this into M/L-sized scope. Worth doing later if user feedback says shortcuts aren't discoverable enough.

UI-05's diff overlay is computed client-side with a per-channel tolerance of 24 (web/src/compare.ts's CHANNEL_TOLERANCE) -- chosen empirically to absorb PNG re-encoding/anti-aliasing noise between two genuinely identical renders without being so loose it would hide a real one-pixel text change. Not derived from engine/verify.py's DEFAULT_TOLERANCE (0.001, a *fraction of pixels*, a different kind of threshold entirely).

UI-05's 'before' image is always the document exactly as first opened (UndoRedoJournal.original_bytes), never 'the state before the most recent edit' -- comparing after two edits shows edit-1+edit-2 combined against the pristine original, not edit-2 in isolation. Matches SPEC.md 8.4's wording; FNT-12 (already built) is the per-edit-diff feature, a different thing.

UI-04's history panel shows only what was requested (an Op's own fields via journal.history/model_dump()), never the EditResult each op produced -- tier, confidence, verification are NOT part of GET .../history's response. Documented in history.ts's module docstring, not a silent gap.

mypy must be run scoped to `engine cli tools server` (matching .github/workflows' own `mypy engine cli tools server`), never over the whole tree -- running it over `tests/` too surfaces ~240 pre-existing errors in test files that were never meant to be strictly typed and are not part of the actual CI gate.

PyMuPDF's Document.tobytes() is NOT idempotent even with zero document changes between calls -- it regenerates a random component of the PDF's /ID array on every single call. Compare parsed content (get_text(), page_count, rendered PNG bytes) instead of raw PDF bytes in any test.

pip-audit in this sandbox flags CVEs in cryptography/httplib2/pip/pyjwt/setuptools/urllib3/wheel -- none are pdfworkerz's own dependencies (confirmed via grep against pyproject.toml). Sandbox environment drift, not something a code change here introduces or can fix.

UI-02's click-to-edit overlay approximates the font family/weight/style shown while editing (a name-based serif/sans/mono+bold/italic guess) rather than loading the document's actual embedded font as a browser @font-face -- documented in web/README.md.

overlay.ts's cancelEdit() has a documented reentrancy fix (contentEditable=false can synchronously fire blur, re-entering cancelEdit) -- take a local copy of the shared 'active box' reference and null the shared one immediately before touching the box, or a future edit to this ordering will reintroduce the crash it fixed.

ReplaceTextOp (search-based) must never be reused for a UI action that targets one specific span the user clicked -- it edits every occurrence of the matched text on the page. ReplaceSpanTextOp (index-based) is what click-to-edit uses instead.

PreviewTextOp/PageSpansOp/render_original_page are read-only and deliberately never journaled -- applied directly in server/app.py, not through the generic POST .../ops + journal.record path. Any FUTURE read-only Op or route should follow the same direct-apply pattern.
viewer.ts's reloadDocument rebuilds the ENTIRE thumbnail rail rather than invalidating just the current page's thumbnail -- a deliberately accepted minor inefficiency, not a bug.

server/app.py's CORSMiddleware is scoped to a loopback-origin regex (127.0.0.1/localhost/::1, any port) -- deliberately permissive on port since auth here is a header a browser never auto-attaches, unlike a cookie. Revisit before ever adding cookie-based or credentialed auth.
web/package.json pins pdfjs-dist==6.3.289 deliberately: versions >=5.6.83 <6.2.108 carry a public high-severity CVE. Re-run npm audit by hand after ever changing this pin.

web/src/polyfills.ts + web/src/pdf.worker.ts work around a real Map/WeakMap.prototype.getOrInsertComputed gap on this sandbox's pinned Playwright test browser. No-op on any browser that already has it natively.

tests/web/'s Playwright tests build on a *built* web/dist, never `vite dev` -- if web/dist doesn't exist, the whole module is skipped (not failed), so a plain `pytest` run with no prior `npm run build` silently produces no UI-0x evidence.

RTL scripts (Arabic, Hebrew) and CJK vertical writing mode are not supported for editing -- documented in tests/engine/test_font_cjk.py's module docstring
fit=True (FNT-10) fragments a span's texttrace into one span per character, breaking a second edit's ability to find that text as one span -- defaults to False
FNT-09's kerning only reads legacy 'kern' tables, not GPOS pair positioning; no GSUB ligature substitution is attempted at all
font-name matching between texttrace and Page.get_fonts()/pikepdf goes through engine.fonts.match.normalize_font_name plus a containment-match fallback
detect_blocks (engine/fonts/blocks.py) assumes its input span list is already in visual top-to-bottom order -- not guaranteed after an edit
ReflowTextOp's overflow check runs before its require_tier check, so an overflowing edit is reported as overflow even when the font match is also weak
